Hand-checked: total flux through any closed surface = (1/ε₀) × net enclosed charge, ∮ E·dS = q/ε₀ — matches NCERT and the book (printed p.19). recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The statement
lines: The total electric flux through any closed
surface is 1/ε₀ times the net charge
steps.margin_note: First mark. Three load-bearing words: closed, net, enclosed.
steps.why: Each word closes a hole: closed makes the flux countable, net allows + and − charges together, enclosed excludes charges outside the surface, which give zero net flux.
common_mistakes: Dropping the word closed. The law holds only for a closed surface.
Saying charge on the surface or near the surface. Only charge ENCLOSED by the surface counts.

recall.must_convey: That the total flux through any closed surface equals the net enclosed charge divided by ε₀.
accept: one by epsilon nought times the charge enclosed
net charge inside divided by epsilon nought
reject: the integral sign with the circle

steps.memory_tip: Closed surface, net charge, enclosed — the three words the mark hangs on.

steps.label: The equation
lines: Here q is the total charge enclosed by the
closed surface S, and ε₀ is the
permittivity of free space. The circle on
the integral sign shows the surface is
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Write the equation and say what q and ε₀ stand for.
steps.why: The equation is the statement in symbols: the left side is the total flux through S, the right side is the enclosed charge over ε₀. Naming q and ε₀ shows the symbols are understood, not copied.
common_mistakes: Writing a plain integral sign instead of the closed-surface integral ∮.
Writing q as any nearby charge. q is the charge INSIDE the surface only.

recall.must_convey: That the equation is the closed-surface integral of E · dS equal to q over ε₀, with q the enclosed charge.
accept: closed integral of E dot dS
reject: flux through any closed surface is one by epsilon nought times the charge

steps.memory_tip: The circle on the integral is the closed surface itself — flux out, charge in.

insider_note: Statement in words plus the equation with q and ε₀ named — the examiner wants both forms, not one.
